D: A veteran catcher is brought in to train a wild young pitcher, and they both catch the eye of the same woman.
P: Serve the snacks when the Durham Bulls take the field.
S: Franks grilled until split, tucked into soft buns with yellow mustard and pickle relish, wrapped in paper like at the stand.
Crash and Nuke killing time in the dugout

Raw peanuts roasted with butter, honey, brown sugar and cayenne until glossy and crunchy, finished with flaky salt and served warm in paper bags. Heat the oven to 170C. Melt 30g butter with 3 tbsp honey, 2 tbsp brown sugar, half a tsp cayenne and 1 tsp salt. Toss with 400g raw unsalted peanuts until coated. Spread on a lined tray and roast 20 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes, until deep golden. Sprinkle with flaky salt and leave to cool on the tray for 10 minutes so they crisp. Break up any clumps and scoop into paper bags.
Little cornmeal and onion fritters fried golden, the Southern side for every ballgame and fish fry.
M: Annie Savoy's house, where the season's lessons happen

Chicken drumsticks soaked overnight in spiced buttermilk, dredged in seasoned flour and fried until crackling, with creamy mash and peppery gravy. Soak 8 drumsticks overnight in 500ml buttermilk with 2 tsp salt and 1 tsp hot sauce. Mix 250g plain flour with 2 tsp paprika, 1 tsp garlic powder, 1 tsp pepper and 1 tsp salt. Dredge the chicken, pressing to coat. Fry in oil at 160C for 12 to 14 minutes until cooked through to 75C inside. Mash 1kg potatoes with butter and milk. For gravy, whisk 2 tbsp of the frying flour into 2 tbsp butter, then 400ml chicken stock and plenty of pepper.
Pork shoulder slow cooked at 150C for 5 hours, pulled and tossed with a tangy vinegar and brown sugar sauce, piled into buns with slaw.
W: Annie's church of baseball, deep in the South

Layers of homemade vanilla custard, sliced banana and soft vanilla biscuits under a thick cap of whipped cream, chilled overnight. Whisk 4 egg yolks, 120g caster sugar and 50g cornflour in a saucepan, then whisk in 750ml milk. Cook over medium heat, stirring, for 6 to 8 minutes until thick. Off the heat, stir in 20g butter and 2 tsp vanilla. Cover the surface and cool. Layer 250g vanilla wafer biscuits, 4 sliced bananas and the custard in a dish, repeating twice. Whip 300ml cream with 1 tbsp icing sugar, spread on top and chill overnight.
K: a warm North Carolina night at the Durham Bulls game

Strong black tea sweetened with brown sugar, cooled and poured over ice with bourbon, fresh lemon and mint, in big ballpark cups. Steep 4 black tea bags in 1L just-boiled water for 5 minutes, remove and stir in 80g brown sugar until dissolved. Cool, then chill for 1 hour. Fill 4 tall glasses with ice. Add 45ml bourbon to each, top with 200ml of the tea and squeeze in a lemon wedge. Slap a mint sprig between your hands and drop it in. Leave out the bourbon for non-drinkers.

s.how: Grill 8 hot dog franks until they split and blister. Tuck each into a soft bun with a stripe of yellow mustard and a spoon of pickle relish. Wrap tightly in paper so the bun steams, then hand them out like the stand behind home plate.

Whisk 1 cup fine cornmeal, 1/2 cup self-raising flour, 1 tbsp sugar and 1 grated onion with 1 egg and 180ml buttermilk. Drop teaspoons into 5cm hot oil and fry for 3 minutes until golden. Drain and serve with butter or hot sauce.

m.how: Rub a 2kg pork shoulder with salt and roast covered at 150C for 5 hours until it pulls apart. Simmer 250ml apple cider vinegar with 3 tbsp brown sugar and chilli flakes and toss through the shredded pork. Pile into buns with shredded cabbage slaw.
